Home · Moonshot

Our moonshot

What if ten times as many kids could learn this?

What if we could teach 10 times more young people to build robots and use AI, without needing 10 times the teachers, rooms, or money?

See the three programsWhat we have done
This is a hope, and we have not done it.Our moonshot

This is a hope, and we have not done it.

What we have done

Programs in Cameroon have run since November 2022, about 4 years. About 5,000 children have trained in holiday programs, and about 3,200 pupils aged 8–15 are at EDUCARE School Bamenda, a partnership running since June 2023. A McKinney pilot of about 30 students followed in 2024.

What we are building

Academy, League, and Innovation Lab are the three programs. The 2027 season in Dallas–Fort Worth scales the 2024 pilot to about 15 teams and about 90 students. A Dallas championship in April 2028 is proposed, and the Global Innovation Challenge has no date yet.

The hope

Teach many more kids without hiring ten times the teachers or renting ten times the rooms. Ideas we may try:

  • A tutor that uses AI
  • Kits that pack small
  • Labs that schools share
  • The learning site
  • The same lessons in every city
  • Training the adults who teach
  • Partners who cover costs
  • Teams in Cameroon and the US working together
